body:
VERIFIED against the code (not merely reported).

`cps/readingservices.py` `handle_annotations` wraps the whole capture block in
`except Exception: log.exception(...)` and then, unconditionally, `return
proxy_to_kobo_reading_services()`. Inside, `dispatch_annotation_sync` does check
the commit — `committed = ub.session_commit(); if committed is False: log.error(...);
continue` — but that failure never reaches the response.

So a member that did not persist still produces an upstream-success PATCH answer.

Why that is terminal rather than merely wrong:
- the Kobo uploads a DELTA, so it never re-offers the annotation;
- `checkforchanges` containment deliberately keeps an owned book out of the
  Kobo-cloud download that could otherwise have healed it.

Note the route already has the right instinct one branch up: when ownership
lookup fails it returns 503 *specifically* so "the device does not treat an
uncaptured upload as successful". The same reasoning is not applied to a
capture that was attempted and lost.

The route docstring also claims the path "persists annotations whenever the
PATCH includes content", which is false for this branch.

OPEN QUESTION before fixing — do not guess: what a Kobo does with a non-success
PATCH is UNOBSERVED. Measured hardware behaviour exists for a 503 on the
annotations *GET* (it empties the device's local set), and that must not be
assumed to transfer to PATCH. Needs a device experiment before a fix ships,
otherwise the cure could be worse than the disease.

---
ADDENDUM 2026-08-21 — two things that change how blocked this is.

1) THE "UNOBSERVED PATCH FAILURE" BET IS ALREADY SHIPPED.
This finding defers a fix because what a Kobo does with a non-success PATCH is
unobserved. But the same route ALREADY returns 503 on PATCH one branch up, when
ownership lookup fails (cps/readingservices.py:476), with the comment "A visible
PATCH failure preserves the opportunity to retry." So the unvalidated assumption
is not merely blocking a proposed fix — it is load-bearing in code that is live
today. The hardware experiment therefore validates SHIPPED behaviour, not just a
candidate fix, which raises its priority rather than gating it behind one.
Whichever way the experiment lands, something changes: either the fix may use a
503, or the existing branch is a latent data-loss risk and must change.

2) THERE IS A FIX DIRECTION THAT NEEDS NEITHER THE EXPERIMENT NOR AN ERROR CODE.
`raw_body = request.get_data(cache=True)` is already read at :456, but it is used
only in-memory, only inside the `elif updated:` branch, to build
`raw_materializations`. It is never persisted before dispatch. Spooling the raw
PATCH body durably BEFORE parsing/dispatch makes a lost capture replayable
server-side, which removes the reason the response code matters at all: the
device may keep its success answer because the server can still recover the
delta. That sidesteps the open question entirely and is independent of it.
Note the existing stage0 raw sidecar is NOT this — it is keyed to an Annotation
row that a successful dispatch already created, so it cannot cover the case where
dispatch itself threw.

Neither point contradicts the original finding; both are additive, and (2) is
implementable now.
title: The annotations PATCH is answered success even when a member failed to commit
